page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-accelerated instructions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES cryptography, and Intel Virtualization Technology.

This instance features a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per core, positioning it within the memory-optimized category. It is equipped with 262 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. The memory subsystem demonstrates average performance, with uncached read bandwidth at 42.22 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 31.07 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 365.97 GB/sec.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between compute power and memory capacity. The server exhibits poor single-core CPU performance and weak multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests. However, it maintains average results in Passmark CPU tests, software compilation, and database operations. LLM inference capabilities are limited, showing average speeds for small 135M models but dropping to poor performance for medium 7B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-8s_v3 offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-heavy workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications with large memory footprints but moderate processing demands.
